original_record.summary: Anonymous GET /elections/{id}/tally/draft synchronously recomputes the full homomorphic aggregate (and after restart/eviction the full proof-verifying ballot analysis) on the single event loop on every call.
original_record.scenario: Once any election has its tally aggregate posted (TALLYING/STALLED/AUDIT/ARCHIVED/IMPORTED), an anonymous client loops GET .../tally/draft; with 2,000 counted ballots each request stalls the whole instance 5.5-6.9 s.
original_record.evidence: PoC packages/server/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts in /home/user/audit/quietvote-b2, `node --test --test-name-pattern=B2-01 test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts`: aggregate 2.659-3.344 ms per counted ballot; 2000 counted -> 409 after 5539-6948 ms with /healthz delayed equally; analyzeBallotLog 116-119 ms per ballot (PoC injects 2,000-ballot set into cached analysis).
original_record.suggested_fix: Serve draft from stored aggregate; return 409 before work when fewer than t shares; cache per (decrypters, shares); move work to a bounded worker queue; consider class P or coordinator-only access.

interim_verification.known: Partly related to NOTES.md:85 (worker-thread proof verification not implemented). That note does not cover recomputing the draft for every anonymous request.
interim_verification.output_excerpt: V=20: draft runs 57/72/101/69 ms, all 409 (no shares posted). V=100: draft runs 319/296/317/253 ms, all 409; aggregate(100)=266 ms; aggregate(2000 counted)=5706 ms (V=20 run: 6255 ms).
interim_verification.refutation_attempt: Read app.ts:410-421. The route is class R with auth 'none', and the handler calls rt.buildTallyDraft(use) synchronously with no await. election.ts:1150-1161 caches the ballot analysis (st.analysis). buildTally (protocol/src/tally.ts:224-228) still calls aggregate(p, counted) and decryptAggregates on every call, before it checks whether enough shares exist. The result is not memoized. The read rate limit is 120/min per IP bucket by default (config.ts:146). At about 2.5-3 ms per counted ballot that is far more blocking time per minute than a minute holds. maxVotersPerElection defaults to 10,000 (config.ts:227), so 2,000 counted ballots is in range. No spec or decision permits this, and QV-29-REQ-019 requires event-loop lag p99 < 100 ms. I did not refute it. I did not reproduce the restart/eviction case (full analyzeBallotLog with proof checks), which costs once per load, nor a real 2,000-ballot election. The 2,000-ballot figure comes from timing the same aggregate() over 2,000 counted ballots. Per-call cost grew roughly linearly from V=20 to V=100. With no shares posted every call returns 409 after doing the full work. In my in-process event-loop histogram, monitorEventLoopDelay showed 0 for most draft calls. Because the handler is synchronous, the blocking is shown by the in-process wall-clock time instead.
interim_verification.notes: For an election in TALLYING/STALLED/AUDIT/ARCHIVED/IMPORTED with an aggregate posted, any anonymous client can repeatedly block the event loop of the whole instance, including elections still open. Link-access elections need the read key. Vote integrity is not affected. Impact is availability. I agree with the suggested fix: serve the stored aggregate and return 409 before doing work.

consolidation_assessment.reproduction: Confirmed in supplied B2 PoC and interim timing verification; consolidation regression makes ensureAnalysis throw and verifies insufficient-share response plus successful draft after runtime eviction without invoking it.

Imported mirrors explicitly refuse this convenience endpoint with 409 rather than trust ignored ballot records. First draft still verifies share proofs/decodes counts; worker isolation and production-scale p99 load measurements remain unfulfilled general requirements.

original_record.summary: POST /imports runs full verifyElection on the event loop and checks ELECTION_EXISTS only after full verification, so a valid bundle can be resubmitted repeatedly to stall the instance.
original_record.scenario: Attacker creates an org (default registrationMode open) and resubmits a large public bundle with new Idempotency-Keys; each submission stalls the instance for full proof verification, then fails ELECTION_EXISTS.
original_record.evidence: PoC B2-02 in packages/server/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts: 6 ballot entries, first import stall 959-1034 ms, duplicate (refused) stall 794-1304 ms via perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay.
original_record.suggested_fix: Check electionAny(manifest.election_id) and quota before verifyElection; verify in a worker with CPU budget; per-org import rate; correct NOTES.md:144.

interim_verification.known: Partly known: NOTES.md:85 lists worker-thread proof verification as not implemented (verification runs on the event loop). NOTES.md:144 says 'Verification (job; yields to the event loop)', which is misleading: verifyElection (protocol/src/verify.ts) only awaits inside adjudicateDkg.
interim_verification.output_excerpt: bundle=160768B. Duplicate import: job failed rule=ELECTION_EXISTS (409), total 1208 ms, max event-loop lag 1003 ms. Same bundle with manifest_hash=000..0: rule=MANIFEST_HASH (422), total 1118 ms, max lag 1052 ms.
interim_verification.refutation_attempt: Read imports.ts:196 (await verifyElection, effectively synchronous) and :323 (the ELECTION_EXISTS check in commitImport runs only after verifyBundle). The ext-routes.ts:90-111 pre-checks cover quota, org and body only. Mitigations that do exist: class X rate limit of 2/hour per IP bucket (config.ts:152), importQueueMax 2, an authenticated org key is required, and registrationMode defaults to 'open' (config.ts:200). These limit the rate but do not stop it. A single submission of a large bundle (up to 64 MiB, maxImportEntries 250k) can stall the instance for a long time. The scenario holds. Checking ELECTION_EXISTS earlier is not a sufficient fix: a bundle that fails a later check (for example a wrong manifest_hash query parameter) also runs the full verification on the event loop before it is refused, as my second case shows.
interim_verification.notes: The underlying cause is synchronous verification on the event loop (a documented gap). The early-check ordering is a secondary issue. NOTES.md:144 should be corrected.

consolidation_assessment.reproduction: Supplied B2 and interim tests confirmed long synchronous import proof verification and duplicate verification before ELECTION_EXISTS; unchanged verifyBundle/commitImport paths remain present.
consolidation_assessment.tests: Existing imports.test.ts still documents duplicate refusal after verification; no new timing claim made.
consolidation_assessment.remaining_review: Need worker/time budget/bounded CPU isolation, early trusted-id/quota preflight, and suitable abuse limits. NOTES now states that yields occur between stages, not within verifyElection. This is a remaining availability blocker.

original_record.summary: instance_admin keys, once seeded, can never be revoked; removing them from adminKeys leaves them active and no API revokes them.
original_record.scenario: Operator removes a compromised admin key from config and restarts; the key still gets 200 on /admin/status and can mint org_owner keys in any org.
original_record.evidence: PoC B2-03 in packages/server/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts: after removal GET /admin/status -> 200; POST /orgs/<org>/keys (org_owner) -> 201.
original_record.suggested_fix: At start, revoke every instance_admin key not in adminKeys with an operator_audit row; document rotation.

interim_verification.output_excerpt: after removal: admin/status=200 mint org_owner=201
interim_verification.refutation_attempt: app.ts:69 only seeds keys. controldb.ts:236-238 seedAdmin inserts a key if it is missing and never revokes one. revokeKey is called only from DELETE /orgs/:org/keys/:keyid (app.ts:265-276), which requires k.org_id === org, and admin keys have org_id NULL, so it returns 404. admin.ts:20 states 'no API creates admin keys', and no API or startup step removes them either. No spec, ADR or NOTES entry says that removing a key from config leaves it active, or describes how to rotate admin keys. D-84 (admin auth model) is still pending and does not address revocation. An admin key can also mint org_owner keys in any org (app.ts:250), which conflicts with QV-12 §5 ('operators cannot add org admins'). That makes the impact of a compromised key larger. I did not refute it. Precondition: the admin key must already be compromised. An operator with database access could revoke it by hand.
interim_verification.notes: Fix: at startup, revoke instance_admin rows that are not in adminKeys and audit-log the revocation.

consolidation_assessment.reproduction: Restart regression seeds admin, verifies access, removes configuration, restarts same persistent data, then observes 401.
consolidation_assessment.tests: consolidation.test.ts B2-03/B2-09; npm test -w @quietvote/server: 140/140 pass (server-tests-final.log)
consolidation_assessment.remaining_review: Removed active instance_admin keys are revoked and operator-audited at startup. Rotation uses a distinct new key; revoked ids are not implicitly reactivated. Operational rotation rehearsal remains advisable before deployment.

original_record.summary: The server evaluates witness quorum with operator config witnesses and ignores manifest bb.witnesses.
original_record.scenario: Manifest names w1 with key W, server config maps w1 to operator key O; W's cosignature is dropped while O's opens the election, gates the aggregate, yields witnessed:true/integrity:ok and clears quarantine.
original_record.evidence: PoC B2-04 in packages/server/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts: manifest witness cosig accepted=[]; operator key accepted=["w1"]; open=201; manifest-policy witnessed=false.
original_record.suggested_fix: Derive per-election policy from manifest bb.witnesses; refuse manifests whose witnesses mismatch config keys; use same policy in clearQuarantine.

interim_verification.known: Related open errata QV-ERR-PY-014 / TODO N-22 (bb.witnesses is not defined in QV-16 §5.6.1). NOTES.md:156(e) documents the same behaviour for imported logs only.
interim_verification.output_excerpt: manifest-witness cosig: 200 {"accepted":[],"rejected":[],"witnessed":false}; open before cfg cosig=409; cfg cosig accepted=["w1"]; state.witnessed=true; open after=201
interim_verification.refutation_attempt: election.ts:254-256 builds the policy from env.witnessPolicy(quorum), which uses the cfg.witnesses keys (app.ts:62, 67). The manifest's bb.witnesses is never read on the live path. election.ts:890 checks only that witness_quorum <= the number of configured witnesses, so a manifest whose witnesses differ from config is accepted (201). By contrast, the import path (imports.ts) and protocol witnessAnchors (logcheck.ts:68) take the manifest witnesses, and QV-18-REQ-020 (Must) says the witnessed status is computed from the manifest. Partial refutation, clearQuarantine only: QV-09 §… (09-api-data-contracts.md:380) explicitly says quarantine/clear names 'configured witnesses', so that sub-claim is spec-permitted. Mitigating factors: QV-16 (the higher authority) does not define bb.witnesses, an open erratum covers it, and verifiers that use the manifest anchors would flag such an election as not witnessed. So the impact is a server gate that disagrees with the manifest, plus manifest-witness cosignatures being dropped silently (they are neither accepted nor rejected). It is not undetectable integrity loss.
interim_verification.notes: Confirmed for the open/aggregate gates and the witnessed/integrity status. The clearQuarantine part is permitted by QV-09. Severity is tempered by the open erratum and by verifier-side detection.

consolidation_assessment.reproduction: Pre-fix regression accepted operator witness with 200; post-fix operator key gets 403 and only manifest-only key opens the election. Policy advertises manifest-only name.
consolidation_assessment.tests: consolidation.test.ts B2-04; negative.test.ts; events.test.ts; admin.test.ts; npm test -w @quietvote/server: 140/140 pass (server-tests-final.log)

Instance configuration is fallback only when the manifest omits a witness list, matching current manifest/import compatibility. External witness monitoring remains absent.

original_record.summary: m-of-k control records (pause/resume/security-notice) have no freshness binding, so a single earlier signer can replay an old record.
original_record.scenario: Coordinators A and B (m=2) pause then resume; A alone re-wraps the old pause record in a new entry header and the OPEN election is paused, ballots refused with 409 (up to maxHalts).
original_record.evidence: PoC B2-05+B2-06 in packages/server/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts: solo pause -> 422 E_SIG; replayed 2-of-3 pause -> 201; ballot while paused -> 409.
original_record.suggested_fix: Bind control bodies to state (after_seq or nonce) and reject bodies whose JCS bytes are already on the log; needs spec definition (G-17).

interim_verification.known: Not found in the prior audits listed (CP/SRV/BC/TR). The auditor's suggested fix references gap G-17, but no G-17 exists anywhere in docs/ at this SHA.
interim_verification.output_excerpt: B2-05 replay=201 ballot-while-paused=409 (solo 1-of-3 pause -> 422; the log holds two notice entries with byte-identical pause bodies)
interim_verification.refutation_attempt: election.ts:741-746 `multi` checks only that m coordinator signatures over (mh, body) are valid and that the entry author is one of the signers. The control body (records.ts:13-18, schema records.ts:33) is {proto,type,action,reason?}. It has no seq, nonce or state binding. vNotice (election.ts:897-930) checks only the current state and maxHalts. The QV-18 header author_nonce (docs/18 §5.3 step 6) stops replay of a whole entry but not re-wrapping a body in a fresh header. The protocol verifier (logcheck.ts:120-228, X-31/X-32) reports control entries but never applies or deduplicates them. No spec or ADR allows replaying a control record. QV-07-REQ-034 requires 'k-of-m threshold enforced', and QV-ADR-022 makes pause/resume a k-of-m steward authority. Not refuted. Limits: the replayer must have signed the original record. The replay is visible on the log. Pauses are capped by maxHalts, but resume can also be replayed, so one earlier signer can un-pause an incident pause.
interim_verification.notes: I signed the genuine pause and resume with coordinators 1 and 2. Coordinator 2 alone (whose solo pause gets 422 E_SIG) re-posted the old pause body: 201, phase PAUSED, and a ballot then got 409. Replaying the old resume also worked. Locations at this SHA are accurate.

consolidation_assessment.reproduction: B2 PoC and interim verification confirmed prior multi-signature control-body replay; controlSchema still lacks signed freshness binding and repeated-body detection.
consolidation_assessment.tests: Original evidence retained in docs/audit/2026-10-28/poc/B2/packages/server/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts.txt; no claim of current fix.
consolidation_assessment.remaining_review: Owner must define freshness binding and replay semantics for repeated legitimate actions. Exact-body dedup alone would prevent identical future notices/resumes and is not silently chosen. Remaining lifecycle/authority blocker.

original_record.summary: election_close is accepted at any time in OPEN/PAUSED with no time check against voting_close.
original_record.scenario: m coordinators close the election 7.5 days before voting_close; voters planning to vote later are disenfranchised.
original_record.evidence: PoC B2-05+B2-06 in packages/server/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts: election_close accepted 7.5 days before voting_close (201); repo's fullElection helper relies on it.
original_record.suggested_fix: Reject election_close while now < voting_close - clock_skew_s.

interim_verification.known: Not in the prior audits listed. The protocol verifier already detects it after the fact (packages/protocol/src/logcheck.ts:598 E_TIME_WINDOW 'early close or late cutoff'), but only when the close is witnessed.
interim_verification.output_excerpt: B2-06 close=201 7.46d early, later ballot=409
interim_verification.refutation_attempt: election.ts:837-844 checks only the marker name and the m-of-k signatures. There is no comparison against manifest voting_close. By contrast, election_open (election.ts:832) does check voting_open. The specs forbid early close: QV-03 §5.5 (docs/03:203) says 'No early close. Close before close_at is impossible except HALT->CANCELLED', and QV-16 §5.14.3 (docs/16:662), which outranks other specs, says 'the coordinator may not close early'. QV-18 §5.2 (docs/18:166) says only 'after opens_at', but QV-16 prevails. No ADR or owner decision permits early close. Not refuted. The close needs m coordinator signatures (the QV-07 A3 malicious-steward threat). With witness_quorum>0 the verifier flags it afterwards. With witness_quorum=0 (the default in the test world) the times are only reported as unwitnessed.
interim_verification.notes: After open at 2026-11-01T10:00Z, a 2-of-3 election-close was accepted 7.46 days before voting_close (2026-11-08T21:00Z). A voter casting one hour later, still inside the published window, got 409. This disenfranchises voters through an authorized but non-conformant action that the server should refuse.

consolidation_assessment.remaining_review: No-early-close gate enforces server now >= signed voting_close without a permissive skew allowance. Tests advance to actual close time. Auto-close scheduler remains absent.

original_record.summary: Restoring an older election DB is not detected and the server signs a second, different root for a size it already signed.
original_record.scenario: Operator restores yesterday's DB (e.g. /admin/backups copy); server appends at already-signed sequence numbers, producing valid fork evidence against its own log key while reporting integrity ok.
original_record.evidence: PoC B2-07 in packages/server/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts: restored DB accepted (integrity=ok); second checkpoint for size 2 signed; checkFork ok=true.
original_record.suggested_fix: Persist last signed (size, root) per election in control.sqlite and optionally poll witnesses at start; refuse append when behind, quarantine.

interim_verification.known: Partly self-disclosed: packages/server/NOTES.md:136-137 says 'Not done: ... a 60 s REQ-053 poll of witnesses (only gossip peers feed the rollback guard)'. Backup/restore drills T-248 and T-250 are Open in docs/plan/TODO.md. Related to TR-03 (trustee-side rollback, unmerged PR #8). Disclosure is not a spec permission.
interim_verification.output_excerpt: B2-07 integrity after restore=ok phase=SETUP; size 2 signed twice with different roots; fork={"ok":true,"value":"fork"}
interim_verification.refutation_attempt: The only rollback guard on load is in board/src/log.ts:73-79, which compares the tree with checkpoints stored in the same DB. Those checkpoints are restored together with the DB, so a coherent older snapshot passes. ElectionRuntime.open (election.ts:145-163) and the control DB keep no last-signed (size, root). Gossip catches it only if gossipPeers are configured and a peer holds the newer note. The tests here and the auditor's PoC run with none. QV-18-REQ-012 (Must, docs/18:77) says 'A server restart shall not change this (persist last checkpoint before replying). Test: restore older DB backup -> server refuses to sign'. REQ-053 and QV-12-REQ-004 / §7 also require failing closed. Not refuted.
interim_verification.notes: Steps: copy the election sqlite at size 1, append ceremony_start, fetch checkpoint A (size 2), stop, restore the copy, restart (integrity=ok), append election_cancel, fetch checkpoint B (size 2). A and B parse with the same size and different roots, and checkFork returns 'fork' under the election log key. Impact: the server produces self-incriminating equivocation evidence and silently drops entries (for example ballots) accepted after the backup. Witnesses or clients holding pins would later detect it.

consolidation_assessment.reproduction: Supplied B2 rollback PoC and interim verification confirmed older election DB restoration can cause the log key to sign a fork. Existing evidence guards rely on optional gossip.
consolidation_assessment.tests: Original rollback PoC preserved; existing gossip/admin tests cover only externally supplied rollback/fork evidence.
consolidation_assessment.remaining_review: Need reviewed independent signed-head/high-water persistence and crash/recovery ordering, plus trusted restoration policy. A new rollback trust design is not silently introduced. Remaining integrity blocker; backup self-check is not rollback detection.

original_record.summary: backup --to stores a relative path verbatim and destroy resolves it against the current cwd, missing the real backup and shredding an unrelated file.
original_record.scenario: backup --to share-backup.qvtb in /x, later destroy from another directory: real sealed backup survives, signed destruction attestation claims backups_removed, and a same-named file in cwd is overwritten and unlinked.
original_record.evidence: PoC B2-08 in packages/trustee/test/b2-audit-poc.test.ts: backups_removed:["share-backup.qvtb"]; real backup still present: true; unrelated file present: false.
original_record.suggested_fix: Store resolve(dest)/realpath at backup; lstat and verify bundle magic/header id before shredding; report not found otherwise.

interim_verification.known: Overlaps TR-08 (info, docs/audit/trustee.md on unmerged branch claude/quietvote-audit-trustee-1): 'destroy overwrites recorded backup paths without checking that the file there is still a QV bundle'. The relative-path and cwd angle is new.
interim_verification.output_excerpt: B2-08 report={"removed":["copy.qvtb"],"missing":[]} realBackupStillThere=true unrelatedFileStillThere=false; attestation body keys=ctx,destroyed_at,j,method,proto,statement,type
interim_verification.refutation_attempt: trustee.ts:759 stores the `dest` string verbatim. At keygen (trustee.ts:148) the bundle path is resolved (home: resolve(path)), but the backup path is not. cli.ts:220-222 passes --to unchanged. destroy (trustee.ts:824) calls shred(b.path), which stat()s, overwrites and unlinks whatever that relative path resolves to in the current cwd (fsutil.ts:51-67), with no magic or header check and no lstat. Not refuted. One correction: the signed attestation does not list backups_removed. That list is only in the unsigned CLI report (cli.ts:237). The signed `method` text does claim 'overwrite+unlink of the encrypted bundle and known backups'. If no same-named file exists in the new cwd, the backup is honestly reported as missing with a manual-check reminder, which matches QV-17 §11.2 step 4 ('list and instruct').
interim_verification.notes: I rate it Low rather than Medium. The harmful path needs a cwd change and an unrelated file with the same name in the new cwd. Without both, the tool reports the backup as missing. When both are present: an unrelated file (possibly another election's backup) is destroyed, the real sealed backup survives, and the report says it was removed. That undermines destruction under ADR-013 and causes data loss. The fix is to store resolve(dest), and to lstat the file and check the bundle magic before shredding.

It never uses lstat and does not check for the QVBUNDL1 magic, so it overwrites whatever the link points to and then unlinks only the link. destroy calls it on every recorded backup path (trustee.ts:824) and on the live bundle (trustee.ts:827). The backup-failure rollback also calls it (trustee.ts:769). debugPlaintext() is still a public method at trustee.ts:938-940 and returns encodeBundle(this.d), the full plaintext state. Trustee is re-exported from the package index (packages/trustee/src/index.ts:8), and no code or test in the repo calls the method. QV-17 §11.2 (docs/17-key-ceremony-trustees.md:335-340) requires crypto-erase of the bundle files and says nothing to allow overwriting files that are not bundles. Mitigating factors: exploiting the symlink needs write access to the backup directory between backup and destroy, which usually means the same user or a shared or removable mount. Overwriting a symlinked real backup is arguably the intended effect. debugPlaintext() can only be reached by in-process code that already holds an unlocked Trustee. The finding's wording 'destroys the symlink target rather than the intended file' is slightly imprecise: shred overwrites the target's contents and also removes the symlink.

interim_verification.refutation_attempt: QV-16 §5.5 item 3 says binary values are lower-case fixed-length hex and 'upper-case hex is rejected, not normalised'. Item 2 allows integers only, and a JSON boolean is not an integer. In verifier-py, _record_schema_ok (election.py:85-132) checks hex case only for roll-commit root and election-open manifest_hash, and checks key sets only for DKG and tally records. ristretto.decode_hex and scalar_decode_hex (ristretto.py:116-121, 144-149) use bytes.fromhex, which accepts upper case. election.py:280 decodes the roll the same way, and dkg.py compares indices with == (True == 1). I confirmed that verifier-py accepts all of these non-canonical forms. The reference rejects them by schema (verify.ts:146-152, :262-333). The ctx values differ, so a malicious trustee or coordinator can make the two verifiers compute different DKG transcripts and verdicts. The values decode to the same bytes, so no tampered tally is accepted.
interim_verification.notes: Divergence confirmed in both directions. verifier-py PASSes a tally or roll with upper-case hex that the reference FAILs, and it accepts non-canonical DKG records that the reference excludes, which gives a different ctx and Q. In a real ceremony the honest trustees run the TS rules and exclude the bad dealer, so verifier-py would FAIL a valid election. I rate it Low rather than Medium: this is a conformance and disagreement problem in a skeleton second verifier, and it gives no path to accepting altered counts.
